entities.summary: Nicholas of Ilok was a Hungarian nobleman and Voivode of Transylvania, who played a crucial role in the politics of the region during the late Middle Ages. Born into a prominent family, Nicholas rose to prominence through his military campaigns and strategic marriages, eventually becoming the titular King of Bosnia in 1471. His reign was marked by a series of power struggles with neighboring kingdoms and the Ottoman Empire, which would eventually lead to the fall of Bosnia to the Ottomans in 1496. Despite his significant influence on the politics of the region, Nicholas of Ilok's legacy is largely overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, such as the Habsburgs and the Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II. Nevertheless, his reign remains an important chapter in the history of the Balkans and the Eastern European region during this period. The strategic marriage of Nicholas to the daughter of the King of Hungary, ensuring the alliance and support of the powerful Hungarian kingdom, is a notable example of his diplomatic efforts.
